summary: The solver-visible core is a real, reachable Terraform provider whose production path crosses provider configuration/preflight, ten managed-resource lifecycles, Ansible task/playbook rendering, process execution, operating-system observation, and Terraform state refresh. Direct inspection shows material branching, validation, error handling, state/identity logic, and cross-component integration rather than constant shells. Resource CRUD contains substantial repeated Terraform-framework scaffolding and the strict-profile LOC margin is narrow, so padding risk is MEDIUM rather than LOW; however the repeated surfaces expose materially different OS-resource semantics and removing roughly a quarter of the core would remove major runtime capabilities or reconciliation behavior. This conclusion is independent of the Complexity Governor/validator verdict.

evidence.observation: Real providerserver entrypoint serves provider.New(version) at registry.terraform.io/local/ansibleops.
Provider configuration creates runtime state, invokes preflight, and registers ten distinct Terraform managed-resource types.
Preflight performs inventory parsing and locality checks, executable resolution, temp-workspace writability probes, and bounded timeout validation with differentiated failure paths.

The process runner materializes ephemeral playbooks, applies environment overrides, enforces a timeout, captures stdout/stderr/exit state, and distinguishes timeout, process-exit, and process-start failures.
Execute, inventory, module builders, task rendering, and playbook rendering form a reachable translation boundary from Terraform resource intent into Ansible execution.
Observation code reads filesystem metadata/digests/symlinks, local users/groups, cron spools, and line/block state to feed resource Read/refresh behavior.
Lifecycle code provides normalization, validation, change sets, identity hashing, fingerprints, and desired-state comparison used across resource paths.

Ten CRUD resource implementations share framework conventions but differ in desired-state fields, Ansible modules, validation, observation, identity, and reconciliation semantics for paths, content/templates, text edits, symlinks, accounts, groups, and cron.
The solver-visible operator workflow builds the provider, performs terraform init/apply against directory and line resources, verifies resulting OS state, and destroys it.

Task-targeted authoring validation associated with the task commit reports profile=large_system_strict and substantive_loc=3081; this numeric/profile evidence is used only as corroboration, not as a copied semantic verdict.

Q6 requires reachable major modules, material branching/state/error/integration, differentiated subsystem responsibilities, cross-component coupling, a meaningful removal test, and rejection of padding.

Q6 must independently trace entrypoints/reachability, distinguish production complexity from noise, evaluate partial-fix traps/removal impact, and not treat a Complexity PASS or raw LOC as sufficient.

do_not_change: Do not treat this Q6 result as a verdict on specification/test alignment, oracle correctness, or other specialist scopes.
Do not reuse this result after any change that alters the packet-bound review_scope_hash.
Do not inflate the solver-visible core merely to increase LOC; repeated Terraform-framework scaffolding was already treated as a padding-risk signal rather than independent complexity.

role_output.SUBSTANTIVE_LOC_ASSESSMENT: The task-targeted report records large_system_strict with 3,081 substantive LOC, 81 above the 3,000 floor. Direct inspection does not count that number as sufficient by itself: a meaningful fraction is repeated Terraform CRUD/schema scaffolding, but the majority of the inspected core participates in distinct provider preflight, resource lifecycle, Ansible translation/execution, observation, identity/normalization, or operator workflow behavior. The narrow margin warrants MEDIUM padding risk, not rejection.
MAJOR_MODULES: Provider entry/configuration/preflight: real Terraform server registration plus runtime validation and dependency injection.
Managed resources: ten Terraform CRUD/import surfaces spanning filesystem objects, copied/rendered content, line/block edits, symlinks, users, groups, and cron.
Ansible translation: inventory inspection, module-specific task construction, deterministic task/playbook rendering, and execution handoff.
Runner/runtime: runtime configuration, temporary-playbook process execution, timeout/error classification, output capture, and environment composition.
Observation/reconciliation: filesystem metadata/digests/link targets, account/group state, cron spool parsing, and text-state inspection used by Reads/refreshes.
Lifecycle utilities: validation, normalization, change tracking, identities, and fingerprints that couple desired configuration to Terraform state.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: A resource lifecycle crosses schema/plan values -> identity/change logic -> Ansible task arguments -> runner execution -> OS state -> observer -> Terraform state; repairing only one layer can leave drift or inconsistent state.
Copy/template behavior couples source/content signals and variables to update decisions, generated Ansible actions, destination observation, and persisted computed state.
User/group behavior spans Terraform desired state, Ansible account arguments, /etc/passwd and /etc/group observation, supplementary-group canonicalization, and identity/state fields.
Provider preflight constraints on inventory, binary, temp workspace, and timeout feed the shared runtime used by every resource, so configuration-path defects can affect all mutations.
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Removing roughly 25% of the core cannot preserve the same operational behavior without replacing equivalent logic: removing the runner/Ansible renderer makes every mutation unreachable; removing observation eliminates drift/refresh state for all resource families; removing provider preflight removes shared runtime safety; removing two or three resource implementations removes entire Terraform-managed OS capabilities. Small helper-only surfaces exist, but they are not a large enough fraction to make the system toy or padding-dominated.
